questions.question: Which is the largest coral reef system in the world?
questions.hint: Stretching over 2,300 km (1,430 miles), Australia's Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest coral reef system and can be seen from space under suitable conditions.

questions.question: Which mammal has the fastest recorded swimming speed?
questions.hint: The Common Dolphin can reach speeds of approximately 60 km/h (37 mph).

questions.question: Which film won the first Academy Award for Best Picture in 1929?
options: All Quiet on the Western Front
questions.hint: Wings (1927) won the first Academy Award for Outstanding Picture at the inaugural ceremony.

questions.question: In the Harry Potter series, what is the name of Harry Potter's owl?
questions.hint: Hedwig is Harry's loyal snowy owl and a memorable companion throughout much of the series.

questions.question: Which organization maintains the global Red List of Threatened Species?
questions.hint: The International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) assesses the conservation status of species worldwide.

questions.question: Which international organization was established through the Bretton Woods Agreement alongside the World Bank?
questions.hint: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) was created in 1944 to promote international monetary cooperation.

questions.question: Which ruler commissioned the Taj Mahal?
questions.hint: The Taj Mahal was built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.question: Which ancient wonder was located in the city of Alexandria?
questions.hint: Also known as the Pharos of Alexandria, it was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

questions.question: Which country invented table tennis?
questions.hint: Table tennis originated in England in the late 19th century as an indoor version of lawn tennis.

questions.question: Which country has won the most Rugby World Cup titles (men's)?
questions.hint: South Africa currently holds the record with four Rugby World Cup titles.

questions.question: Which country has the largest number of natural lakes?
questions.hint: Canada contains more lakes than the rest of the world's countries combined.

questions.question: Which mountain range forms the traditional boundary between Europe and Asia?
questions.hint: The Ural Mountains are widely accepted as part of the conventional boundary between Europe and Asia.

questions.question: Which scientist discovered penicillin?
questions.hint: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928, revolutionizing the treatment of bacterial infections.

questions.question: Which is the hardest naturally occurring substance?
questions.hint: Diamond ranks highest on the Mohs hardness scale with a value of 10.

questions.question: Which country is the birthplace of the Olympic Games?
questions.hint: The ancient Olympic Games originated in Olympia, Greece, in 776 BC.

questions.question: Which writing system is used for the Japanese language alongside Hiragana and Katakana?
questions.hint: Kanji consists of characters of Chinese origin and is one of the three scripts used in modern Japanese writing.

questions.question: Which animal has the largest eyes of any living creature?
questions.hint: The Colossal Squid has the largest confirmed eyes of any known living animal, reaching up to about 27 cm (11 inches) in diameter.

questions.question: Which country is home to the world's largest salt flat, Salar de Uyuni?
questions.hint: Salar de Uyuni covers over 10,000 square kilometers, making it the largest salt flat on Earth.

questions.question: Which particle has the smallest known positive electric charge?
questions.hint: An up quark carries a charge of +2/3e, while a proton and positron each have a charge of +1e. Quarks are not observed in isolation due to confinement.

questions.question: Which civilization first developed a positional decimal number system including the concept of zero?
questions.hint: Ancient Indian mathematicians developed the decimal place-value system and formalized the use of zero, which later spread worldwide through Arabic scholarship.
